title: Klimp (Almond Dumplings)
description: Prepared with almonds, butter, and flour.
steps: Fry the butter and flour for 2 minutes.
Thin with the milk and let the mixture boil while stirring for 10 minutes.
Add the sugar, the blanched and grated almonds and the whisked eggs, and let the mass simmer over heat until it becomes appropriately thick.
Pour the dumpling into a rinsed cloth and let it cool.
Loosen it carefully at the edge, turn it out onto a plate or onto a round dish and serve with broth.

title: Klimp (Semolina Dumplings)
description: Prepared with bitter almonds, sweet almonds, and butter.
steps: Brown the butter and flour together, gradually thin with the milk, and let the mixture cook for 15 minutes
Lift the pan from the side of the heat; add the blanched and grated bitter almond, sugar and the whisked eggs
Let the klimp simmer over heat until it becomes thick
Cool it in a water-rinsed mold and turn it out once it has cooled
When served with fruit soup, garnish with the blanched sweet almond cut into strips
When used with bouillon, garnish with chopped parsley

title: Klimp (Swedish Dumpling)
description: Prepared with almonds, butter, and flour.
steps: Melt butter and flour together for 2 minutes
Add the milk and let the mixture cook while stirring for 10 minutes
Add the sugar, the blanched and grated almonds, and the beaten eggs and let the mass simmer over the fire until it becomes appropriately thick
Pour the klimp into a water-rinsed mold and let it cool
Carefully loosen it at the edge, turn it out onto a plate or round dish and serve with bouillon or meat soups
If desired, sprinkle it with 1 tablespoon chopped parsley when used with bouillon, otherwise garnish it with 20 g blanched sweet almonds, cut into strips

title: Knäck (Brittle, about 100 pieces)
description: Prepared with sweet almonds, cream, and syrup.
steps: Blanch the almonds and chop them finely.
In a pot, beat together the cream, syrup, and sugar and let it cook while stirring until the mass, when tested in cold water, shows a tendency to set (about 25 minutes).
Then add the finely crushed rusks and let the mass cook an additional 5 minutes.
Stir in the almonds and let the mass come to a rapid boil.
Pour it into small pleated paper molds.

title: Knäckebröd, utan jäst (Crisp Bread without Yeast)
description: A bread preparation made with wheat flour, rye or rye flour, and sugar.

ingredients.name: rye sifted or coarse rye flour
ingredients.sourceText: 200 grams rye sifted or coarse rye flour

steps: Sift the flour into a bowl and mix with sugar and salt.
Distribute the butter in flakes in the flour and work in with fingertips.
Add enough milk to make a reasonably firm dough that is worked until smooth, glossy and pulling away from the bowl.
Roll out the dough very thin, prick lightly, and cut with a pastry wheel along a ruler into oblong squares.
Place on buttered sheets and bake light brown in a not-too-hot oven.
Good for envelopes and open-faced sandwiches.

title: Knäckkakor (Crisp Cookies)
description: A biscuit made with wheat flour, baking powder, and butter.
steps: Sift the flour, set aside one kkp for dusting, and mix the rest well with the baking powder
Wash the butter and stir it with the sugar for about 15 minutes
Add the eggs, one at a time
Add the flour and work the dough until it is even and smooth
Cover and let rest for about 2 hours
Roll out to 3 mm thickness, prick well and cut out into small round cookies with a hole on one side
Place on buttered baking sheet and bake until golden brown in a not-too-hot oven

title: Kokning av fisk (Boiling Fish)
description: Prepared with fish, salt, and water.

ingredients.name: Salt (2 teaspoons/10 grams per kilogram of fish)
ingredients.sourceText: Salt (2 teaspoons/10 grams per kilogram of fish)

ingredients.name: Coarse salt (7 grams per liter of water)
ingredients.sourceText: Coarse salt (7 grams per liter of water)

steps: For large whole fish, rub with salt (2 tsp/10 grams per kg fish)
Place fish on a sieve in a fish kettle and add enough cold water so it covers the fish evenly
If no fish kettle is available, invert a bowl on the bottom of another kettle, spread a coarse towel over it, and place the fish on the towel so it can be easily lifted out when done without breaking
Measure the water before adding to the kettle and add 7 grams of coarse salt per liter of water
Cover the kettle, bring water to a rapid boil and skim well
Move the kettle to the side of the stove and finish cooking the fish while the water only simmers gently, allowing 15-20 minutes per kilogram of fish
For small fish or fish cut into slices, place in boiling salted water, skim, then move kettle to the side and finish cooking as described above
Once cooked, immediately transfer fish to a platter with a sieve or on a napkin, garnish with parsley, and serve with sauce made from the cooking liquid or another fine sauce

title: Kokning av flottyr (Making Rendered Fat)
description: Prepared with kidney, pork fat, and potato.
steps: Cut the tallow and fat into fine cubes and let soak in water for about 24 hours
Squeeze the cubes well and put on to cook in new, cold water
Peel and halve a potato or apple and add to the fat, which will thereby become clearer
Let the fat cook until a thin, bluish smoke rises from the surface and the cubes (the "cracklings") sink to the bottom
Strain into a clean earthenware crock and store in a cool place
Note: Fat can also be made from kidney tallow alone but will be harder

title: Kokning av Flottyr (Rendering of Lard)
description: Prepared with kidney, pork fat, and potato.
steps: Cut the fat and lard into cubes; remove all glands and coarser membranes carefully.
Place the cubes in plenty of water and let them sit for 2 days, changing the water once during this time.
Squeeze out the fat well and place it together with 1/2 liter cold water to cook in a high iron pot. The lid should remain on the pot for the first hour.
Peel the potato, cut it in half, and let it cook with the lard, which becomes clearer thereby.
The lard is done cooking when the membranes ("the countesses"), which enclosed the fat, sink to the bottom and it gives off a thin smoke with a characteristic smell of lard.
Remove the pot from heat and after 10 minutes, strain the lard through a sieve or coarse cheesecloth into a stone crock and store in a cool place. This amount yields approximately 2 kg.

title: Kokning i Flottyr (Cooking in Lard)
description: Prepared with lard.

ingredients.name: Lard (rendered fat), heated to approximately 160 degrees C.
ingredients.sourceText: Lard (rendered fat), heated to approximately 160 degrees C.

steps: Use an iron or copper pot for cooking in lard, preferably round in shape and sufficiently deep so that items placed in it have good space to come into contact with the lard, even if the pot is only half filled with it.

Heat the lard until a thin smoke rises from its surface, which indicates it is approximately 160 degrees C. You can also test if the lard is hot enough by placing a hard piece of bread in it, around which a mass of small bubbles will immediately form.
Place what is to be cooked in the lard, not too much at once so that the lard does not cool down, and cook until it becomes golden brown. Place it on gray paper so that the lard drains off well.
Leftover lard can be used several times if it is reheated in water or milk. When it has solidified, scrape off all sediment from the bottom lightly.

title: Kokosbröd (Coconut Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with coconut, eggs, and sugar.
steps: Separate egg yolks and whites
Stir the egg yolks and 1 egg white with the sugar to a foam
Beat the remaining egg whites to stiff peaks and blend into the batter together with the grated coconut
Form the mass into small round cakes, and bake these on well-buttered baking sheets in very weak oven heat

title: Kokt braxen (Boiled Bream)
description: Prepared with bream, peppercorns, and bay leaves.
steps: Scale and clean the fish (see page 171); the head may remain but must be freed from gills.
Rub it with salt and let it rest for 1 hour.
Boil it afterwards either whole or in pieces as in recipe no. 327; when the fins come loose easily, it is done.
The bream can be served either hot or cold.
If served hot, it should be boiled whole, placed on a napkin and garnished with parsley.
If served cold, it is boiled in pieces and the stock is strained over the arranged fish and allowed to set into jelly.
Whether warm or cold, serve it with cold horseradish sauce.

title: Kokt fruktpudding (Boiled Fruit Pudding)
description: A pudding made with apples, apricots, and prunes.

ingredients.name: For the form: 2 dcl. granulated sugar
ingredients.sourceText: For the form: 2 dcl. granulated sugar

steps: The fruit is rinsed very well in several lukewarm waters and is left to lie in cold water overnight.
From this water and the sugar, a clear, simmering syrup is cooked; in it the apples are cooked first, then the apricots and finally the prunes, after they have been pitted.
The syrup is cooked until it is simmering, and is poured over the fruit.
The granulated sugar is melted with stirring in a pan, diluted with boiling water, and with this a smooth, shallow baking form is lined.
When the fruit is cold, it is layered in the form.
The eggs and cream are whipped together and poured over the fruit.
The pudding is baked in a water bath in the oven for about 1 hour, or until the egg mixture has set.
It is removed, loosened from the edge and turned out after 15 minutes.
Served preferably cold, if desired, with whipped cream or vanilla sauce.

title: Kokt Färsk Oxtunga (Boiled Fresh Beef Tongue)
description: Prepared with beef tongue, peppercorns, and carrot.
steps: Clean the tongue and soak it in water for a couple of hours.
Place it in boiling water, which should just cover it, skim well, and add the spices and the carved carrot.
Let the tongue cook slowly for 2 1/2-3 hours, or until the skin can be easily pulled off.
After the skin is removed, place it back in the broth to keep it warm until serving.
Slice the tongue on the bias into 1/2 cm thick slices, arrange them so that the tongue appears whole on the platter at serving.
Garnish with parsley or salad and serve with cooked or stewed vegetables or with a sauce, such as brown mushroom, morel, or olive sauce, and potatoes.
Leftovers of cooked tongue can be sliced, dipped in egg and breadcrumbs, and fried in butter.

They can also be served in brown caper sauce made from 4 dcl meat stock, 1-2 tsp cornstarch, 1 tbsp finely chopped capers, 1/2 tbsp Madeira, salt, and sugar. When the sauce has boiled for 5 minutes, add the tongue slices and let them boil for 5 minutes. Serve with browned potatoes as a breakfast dish.

title: Kokt gädda (Boiled Pike) (for 6 persons)
description: Prepared with pike, vinegar, and salt.
steps: Clean the pike, but do not scale it.
Rinse it well, dry it with a cloth and rub it with the vinegar and salt.
Bend the fish so that head and tail meet, and place it with the back upward in hot, but not boiling water (short broth).
When the broth comes to a boil, skim it, and let the fish simmer slowly at the side of the fire until the fins come loose, or for approximately 1/2 hour.
Place the pike on the serving platter, garnish with a few sprigs of parsley and serve with clarified butter and grated horseradish or with simple fish sauce or milk sauce with horseradish.
The liver can be saved (except during spawning season) and cooked with the fish, then cut up and used as garnish for the fish.

title: Kokt hamburgerbringa (Boiled Hamburg Beef Brisket)
description: Prepared with beef and water.

ingredients.name: salted and smoked beef brisket
ingredients.sourceText: 3 kg. salted and smoked beef brisket

steps: Brush the brisket well with lukewarm water, crack it and let it soak in plenty of cold water for approximately 12 hours.
Place it in cold water, bring it quickly to a boil, skim well and cook as in recipe 497.
Let the brisket remain in its broth for 1/2 hour before serving, as it will thereby become more tender.
Serve, cut into even, beautiful slices, with vegetables, vegetable pastries and some of the broth, mixed with a little good broth, or also with mixed meat dishes.

The finest is considered cold Hamburg brisket. It is then allowed to cool in the broth, cut into thin slices, which are arranged on a base of dark gelée and garnished with gelée in molds or gelée croutons and parsley. Serve with potato or vegetable salad.

Rub it with the lemon and cook with 10 g salt per litre of water for approximately 1/2 hour as in recipe no. 327
Let it drain, place on a warm platter, garnish with fluted lemon slices and parsley and serve with caper sauce or hollandaise and boiled potatoes

title: Kokt helgeflundra (Boiled Whole Halibut) (for 6 persons)
description: Prepared with halibut, vinegar, and salt.
steps: Wash the fish, scald the dark side with hot water and scrape it well.
Rub it with the vinegar and 1 tbsp. salt, then let it lie in heavily salted water for 1 hour (about 2 tbsp. salt to each liter of water).
Take up the fish and place it on the fire in hot, but not boiling water (short broth) and skim it well when the broth comes to a boil.
Let it simmer slowly at the side of the fire for approximately 1/2 hour.
Place it immediately on the serving platter and garnish with parsley and lemon.
Halibut is served with hard-boiled, chopped eggs and clarified butter or with Hollandaise sauce.

title: Kokt höns (Boiled Chickens)
description: Prepared with chickens, lard, and chicken or veal or broth.
steps: The chickens are plucked, singed, and cleaned (see page 299 onwards), rinsed thoroughly, and left to soak in water for 6 hours.
They are removed, dried inside and out with a cloth, rubbed with salt, trussed (see page 300), covered with lard, which is fastened with fine sail thread previously dipped in boiling water.

The chickens are placed in a pot that should not be wider than to just fit them, the cold broth is poured in, brought to a boil, and skimmed well, after which the onion, parsley, and spices are added.
The chickens should then not boil but only lie in the broth, which should be kept at approximately 90°, until tender, or 2-3 hours, depending on the age of the chickens.
They are removed and kept warm in a water bath.
The broth is reduced and from it is prepared a light mushroom, truffle, tomato, or oyster sauce.
The chickens are cut and arranged on the platter so that they appear whole, garnished with salad, parsley, and, if desired, with slices of truffle or mushroom caps, sautéed in butter.
Served with rice or boiled potatoes. The sauce is served in a sauce boat.

title: Kokt Kalvbringa (Boiled Veal Breast)
description: Prepared with veal, peppercorns, and water.
steps: Prepare the veal breast (see page 232), break it well, place it in boiling water and skim thoroughly, then add the spices.
Let it simmer slowly with a tightly closed lid until it is tender and the outer bones loosen, about 1 1/2–2 hours.
Remove it, take away all loosened bones, and cut the veal breast into beautiful, even pieces, which are placed on a plate and kept warm.
Skim the broth thoroughly and use it for sauce.
For veal breast, one can serve crayfish sauce, oyster sauce, light mushroom sauce, morel sauce, caper sauce, olive sauce, tomato sauce, or dill sauce along with boiled potatoes.
If the veal breast is served with crayfish sauce, it should be garnished with fresh crayfish tails and fresh asparagus, boiled in the meat broth.

title: Kokt kalvhuvud (Boiled Calf's Head)
description: Prepared with calf's head, peppercorns, and carrot.
steps: Split the calf's head (remove the tongue and brain; the tongue is cooked with the head, the brain is used for a stew, see no. 107), rinse and soak in water overnight.

Clean it well, place it along with the tongue in boiling water and skim; add the spices, the blanched carrot, the lemon slices (freed from seeds), the peeled onion and parsley, then let the meat cook until tender.
Remove the head and let it cool; separate the meat from the bones and cut it into even pieces. Strain and skim the broth.

Melt the butter, slice the mushrooms and fry them in the butter until clear, then remove them with a spoon and fry the flour with the butter for 2 minutes, add the meat broth and mushroom broth and let the sauce simmer for 5 minutes.
Finish with egg yolk, add the cut meat and mushrooms, season with spices and a little wine if desired.
Place on a warm platter, sprinkle with parsley and serve with boiled potatoes.

title: Kokt Köttpudding (Boiled Meat Pudding)
description: A pudding made with meat, rusks, and white pepper.

ingredients.name: 400 gr. boneless, cooked or roasted meat
ingredients.sourceText: 400 gr. boneless, cooked or roasted meat

ingredients.name: 1/2 msk. butter for the mold (10 gr.)
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 msk. butter for the mold (10 gr.)

ingredients.name: 2 msk. crushed rusks for the mold
ingredients.sourceText: 2 msk. crushed rusks for the mold

steps: Chop the meat very finely (do not grind) and mix with the milk, rusks, and beaten egg yolks, then let the mixture stand for 1 hour to swell; if it is then too stiff, add a little more milk.
Add the butter, spices, cucumber, and onion (fried in butter), and taste the mixture carefully.
Finally fold in the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks.
Pour the mixture into a buttered and breadcrumb-lined baking pan and bake the pudding in a water bath in the oven for about 1 1/2 hours.
Turn out onto a serving dish and garnish with slices of tomatoes or cucumber and parsley.
Serve with pan sauce, meat gravy, or melted butter. If desired, the cucumber and onion can be omitted.

title: Kokt Lammbringa (Boiled Lamb Breast with Dill)
description: Prepared with lamb, water, and salt.
steps: Break the breast well, dry it with a cloth, wring it out in hot water, place it in boiling water, skim well, salt it and add the dill or parsley.
Let it thereafter cook slowly with a tightly closed lid for 1 1/2-2 hours.
Remove it and cut into beautiful, even pieces, which are placed on a warm platter and garnished with dill or parsley.
Strain the broth, skim it well and use it for sauce and for simpler soups.
Serve boiled lamb breast with dill sauce or with caper or light mushroom sauce. In the former case cook the breast with dill, in the latter case with parsley.

title: Kokt Piggvar (Boiled Turbot)
description: Prepared with fish, lemon, and salt.
steps: Clean the fish, rinse them well in several waters and dry them with a fish towel.
Leave the head on and cut off the gills.
Polish the fins but do not cut them off.
Make a deep incision along the backbone on the dark side of the fish so that the white skin on the other side does not crack.
Rub the fish inside and out with the lemon juice and salt and let them rest for 1 hour, then dry them again.
Place them on a fish steamer with the white side up and cook as in no. 327.
The fish will be whiter if you cook it in 2/3 water and 1/3 milk with 7 g coarse salt to each liter of liquid.
Place the turbot on a napkin, garnish with parsley and beautifully cut lemon wedges and serve with hollandaise, crayfish, or lobster sauce.

title: Kokt potatis (Boiled Potatoes)
description: Prepared with potatoes, water, and salt.
steps: Brush the potatoes, peel with thin peels and rinse well, and let them soak in water until they are to be cooked.
Place in cold water, just enough so it comes to the surface of the potatoes, salt and let simmer slowly until tender (about 20-30 minutes).
Pour off the water, place a cloth over, and shake the potatoes.
Potatoes can also be cooked unpeeled, in which case they only need to be brushed and rinsed well.
New potatoes should be placed in warm water when cooking.
The potatoes turn out best if cooked in steam in a so-called potato cooker.

title: Kokt Rimsaltad Fårbringa (Boiled Brined Lamb Breast)
description: Prepared with lamb, saltpetre, and salt.
steps: Crack the ribs and rub the breast with a mixture of salt, saltpetre and sugar.
Place it in a deep dish and let it stand 3—4 days, turning it frequently in the brine that forms.
Wash the meat thoroughly with a cloth dipped in cold water.

Place in cold water, bring quickly to the boil, skim well and cook for 15 minutes at 100°, after which cool the liquid to 82°-83° and let the meat rest in it without boiling until tender, about 1 1/2-2 hours.
Serve with browned turnips, stewed vegetables or potato purée. The broth can be used for soup or purée.

Alternatively, once cooked, the meat can be brushed with beaten egg, sprinkled with finely crushed breadcrumbs, placed in a baking pan whose bottom is covered with broth, and put in a warm oven to gratinée for 15—20 minutes. Serve as above.

title: Kokt ris (Boiled Rice)
description: Prepared with rice, water, and salt.
steps: Rinse the rice in cold water, add to boiling salted water and let boil vigorously for 15 min., then pour into a colander, rinse with cold water and let drain.
Put the rice in a saucepan, distribute the butter in flakes and blend it into the rice with a fork.
Place the lid on the saucepan, which should then stand in a warm oven for about 15 min., during which the rice is often stirred with a fork.
Serve with eggs, cold fish, boiled meat and chicken.

title: Kokt rödspotta (Boiled Red Bream)
description: Prepared with bream, vinegar, and salt.
steps: For cooking, choose large red breams
Place them on a dish, brush with a little vinegar, let them rest for 1/2 hour, then scrape them well with a knife
Remove the gills and the innards through an incision made at the head
Carefully scrape away the dark membrane and cut off the fins
Rinse the fish very well, dry it, rub it with salt and let it rest for 1 hour, then dry it again
Cook it as in recipe no. 327 and requires great attention during cooking, as it is done in a few minutes
Place on a warm dish with the white side up, garnish with parsley and serve with wine sauce, parsley sauce, or crayfish sauce
Halibut is cleaned and cooked in the same way but requires longer cooking time. Serve with melted butter, grated horseradish and boiled potatoes

title: Kokt Rött Vinbärsgelé I (Cooked Red Currant Jelly I)
description: Prepared with currants, water, and sugar.

ingredients.name: 3/4 to 1 kg sugar per kilogram of juice
ingredients.sourceText: 3/4 to 1 kg sugar per kilogram of juice

steps: Rinse the currants and allow them to drain.
Strip the berries and cook them with the water on very low heat for approximately 20 minutes, stirring.
Pour the berries into a cheesecloth and allow the juice to drip without pressing.
Weigh the juice, add the sugar and stir until the sugar is somewhat melted.
Bring slowly to a boil and allow to cook slowly for 8-10 minutes.
Skim the jelly well during cooking.
Immediately pour into warm jars rinsed with cognac.

title: Kokt salt fårkött (Boiled Salted Lamb)
description: Prepared with lamb and water.
steps: If the meat is too salty to boil directly, soak it the day before.
Break into suitable pieces which should still hang together, and place in cold water (short broth).
When the broth boils, skim well.
If it tastes too salty, pour it off and add new cold water.
Let the meat boil until tender or about 2 hours.
Serve with fried roots, root purée or potato purée.

description: Prepared with ox tongue and water.
steps: Rinse the ox tongue well and place it in cold water.

Remove it from the pot and immediately strip off the skin.
Slice the tongue and serve with peas.

title: Kokt sill med smör och ägg (Boiled Herring with Butter and Egg)
description: Prepared with butter, herrings, and water.
steps: Soak the herring in water the day before it is to be used.
Remove the herring, free it from skin and entrails, and split it down the middle, then remove the backbone and as many small bones as possible.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, peel and chop finely.
Lay the herring in boiling water and let it boil 3-5 minutes, then lay it on a warm platter, alternating with the chopped eggs. The top layer should be eggs.
Melt the butter and pour over, and serve the dish with boiled potatoes.

title: Kokt sill med smör och ägg (Boiled Herring with Butter and Egg)
description: Prepared with butter, salt or fat or herrings, and water.

ingredients.name: 2 large or 4 small salt fat herrings
ingredients.sourceText: 2 large or 4 small salt fat herrings

steps: Soak the herring in water for 12 hours, changing the water 2 times
Skin, remove the insides, fillet down the middle, then remove the backbone and all small bones
Rinse the fillets well and wrap in a fish towel
Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in water and peel; separate the whites and yolks and chop each separately
Place the herring in boiling water with a few sprigs of dill and boil 8-10 minutes
Place on a warm serving dish with a slotted spoon, pour the clarified butter over and garnish the herring with stripes of egg white and yolk
Serve with freshly boiled potatoes as a breakfast dish

title: Kokt sparris (Boiled Asparagus)
description: Prepared with asparagus, water, and salt.
steps: Peel the asparagus, rinse in cold water, and tie together in bundles with all heads pointing the same direction.
Place in boiling, salted water and let boil for 15-20 minutes.
When the asparagus is done, remove it immediately and let it drain.
Place it on an asparagus platter, napkin, or on a large slice of toasted bread dipped in the water in which the asparagus was cooked.
Serve with clarified butter.

title: Kokt Sparris (Boiled Asparagus)
description: Prepared with asparagus, water, and salt.
steps: Scrape the asparagus carefully with a sharp knife toward the tip without touching it; remove only the outermost skin
Rinse the asparagus carefully in cold water
Tie the asparagus into five bundles with the tips facing the same direction
Boil the water with the salt and skim well
Add the asparagus and cook for 15-20 minutes, depending on the nature of the asparagus
Remove immediately and let drain on a sieve or cloth
Place the asparagus on a platter with a folded napkin, cut the strings and remove them
Serve very hot with melted butter arranged as small rolls in a sauce boat, or with a sauce such as true hollandaise, mousseline or béarnaise sauce

title: Kokt sparris (Boiled Asparagus)
description: Prepared with asparagus, water, and salt.
steps: Asparagus is harvested from mid-May to the end of June.
It can be preserved for 4-5 days in a cellar if bundled in bunches and covered with sand.
The largest are served boiled as a side dish; the smaller ones are used for soups and stewed dishes.
Scrape the asparagus carefully with a sharp knife against the tip without touching it; only remove the outermost skin.
Rinse it carefully in cold water, tie it together in five bunches with the tips all pointing the same way.
Bring the water to a boil with the salt and skim it well, then add the asparagus and let it boil for 15-20 minutes, depending on the quality of the asparagus.
Remove it immediately and let it drain on a sieve or cloth.
Place the asparagus on a serving plate with a folded napkin and cut the strings off.
Serve it very hot with melted butter.

title: Kokt vitkål till kött (Boiled White Cabbage with Meat)
description: Prepared with cabbage, carrots, and onion.

ingredients.name: water, 1 tablespoon salt (15 g) for blanching
ingredients.sourceText: 3 liters water, 1 tablespoon salt (15 g) for blanching

steps: Remove all green leaves from the cabbage head; loosen the remaining leaves from the core and remove the thickest part of the main nerve.
Blanch the cabbage leaves (place in boiling salted water and let cook without a lid 5–8 minutes); lift out with a slotted spoon and let drain on cloth.
Roll the leaves into balls and twist them in a cloth.
Butter a saucepan and cover the bottom with the peeled and thickly sliced carrots, the onion, and the pork slice.
Place the cabbage balls on top, sprinkle with the seasonings, add the water, and let cook slowly with a lid until quite tender, about 2½ hours.
Serve as a garnish around meat or on a separate plate.

title: Kokt, Brynt Färsk Oxbringa (Boiled and Browned Fresh Beef Brisket)
description: Prepared with beef, celery, and carrot.
steps: Wash the brisket with a cloth dipped in hot water, rub in the salt, and let sit until the next day
Break the meat well and place in enough boiling water to cover it well

Cut the brisket into nice pieces and garnish with sliced carrot
Strain the sauce and skim it

title: Kokt, Brynt Lammbringa (Boiled and Browned Lamb Breast)
description: Prepared with lamb, carrots, and turnip.

ingredients.name: For the rice: 2 deciliters rice grains
ingredients.sourceText: For the rice: 2 deciliters rice grains

steps: Treat and cook the breast as in the previous recipe but remove it when it is half-tender, or after 45 minutes.
Prepare the vegetables and cut them into strips or beautiful pieces with a vegetable knife or vegetable iron; peel the onion and chop it coarsely.
Remove the breast and cut into even, beautiful pieces. Strain the broth and skim it.

Brown the onion in half of the butter together with the meat, then place it in a saucepan and add 1/2 liter of the broth. Brown the vegetables in the rest of the butter and place them on top of the meat, then let everything cook until soft.
Cook the rice grains as in the previous recipe and arrange them in a pyramid on a round serving platter. Arrange the meat and vegetables in groups around it and garnish the arrangement with parsley.
Strain the broth, skim it, let it come to a boil, season to taste and serve in a sauce boat.

Prepare the vegetables and cut them into strips or beautiful pieces with a vegetable knife or vegetable iron; peel the onion and chop it coarsely.
Remove the breast and cut it into even, beautiful pieces. Strain the stock and skim it.

Brown the onion in half of the butter together with the meat, then place it in a pot and add 1/2 liter of the stock. Brown the vegetables in the remaining butter and lay them on top of the meat, then let everything cook until soft.
Cook the rice grains as in the previous recipe and arrange them in a pyramid on a round serving platter, arrange the meat and vegetables in groups around it, and garnish the dish with parsley.
Strain the stock, skim it, let it come to a boil, season it, and serve it in a sauce bowl.

title: Kokt, färsk oxbringa (Boiled Fresh Beef Brisket)
description: Prepared with brisket, water, and salt.

ingredients.name: middle brisket (or 1 1/2 kg. middle chuck)
ingredients.sourceText: 1 1/2 kg. middle brisket (or 1 1/2 kg. middle chuck)

steps: Dry the brisket with a cloth wrung out in hot water, crack it well, roll it together and bind it, so that it will take less room and be easier to turn.

Place it in boiling water, which is skimmed well when it comes to a boil, add the salt and let the brisket cook slowly with a tight lid until it is tender and the bones easily come loose, or approximately 2 1/2-3 hours.
Take it immediately out of the broth, cut into beautiful pieces, garnish with parsley and serve with boiled potatoes and horseradish-, caper-, or olive sauce.
The broth is used for purée or simpler soups.

The brisket can also, after it is cooked, be placed in a long pan with the meat side up, a little of the broth is added and the brisket is browned in the oven until it has taken on a beautiful brown color. It is then cut and served with potato purée and the broth in the pan, which is strained and skimmed. If the meat is desired to be fatter, use the front brisket.

title: Kokt, Färsk Oxtunga (Boiled Fresh Beef Tongue)
description: Prepared with beef tongue, peppercorns, and carrot.
steps: Clean the tongue and soak it in water for a couple of hours.
Place it in boiling water, which should come just to the top of it, skim well, and add the spices and the prepared carrot.
Let the tongue simmer slowly for 2 1/2 to 3 hours, or until the skin can be easily pulled off.
After removing the skin, place the tongue back in the cooking liquid to keep it warm until serving.
Slice the tongue diagonally into 1/2 cm thick slices, arranging them so that the tongue appears whole on the plate when served.
Garnish with parsley or salad and serve with boiled or stewed vegetables or with a sauce, such as brown mushroom, morel, or olive sauce, and potatoes.
Leftover boiled tongue can be sliced, dipped in egg and breadcrumbs, and fried in butter.

Alternatively, serve in brown caper sauce made from 4 dl meat broth, 1-2 teaspoons cornstarch, 1 tablespoon finely chopped capers, 1/2 tablespoon Madeira, salt, and sugar. After the sauce has boiled for 5 minutes, add the tongue slices and boil for 5 minutes. Serve with browned potatoes as a breakfast dish.

title: Kokt, Griljerad Skinka (Boiled, Grilled Ham)
description: Prepared with ham, egg white, and mustard.
steps: The ham, which should have lain in brine (see Salting of Meat) for 3-4 weeks, is rinsed and left to soak in plenty of cold water for about 12 hours, so that the salt is drawn out.
Place it with rind side up in enough cold water to cover it well.
Let the water come to a boil quickly, skim and let it boil for 15 minutes at 100°.
Cool the liquid thereafter to 82°-83°, and at this temperature let the ham lie for about 3 1/2 hours, or until it is tender, which is tested with a whisk (see page 233).
Place the ham in a deep dish, pour the liquid over, and let the ham cool in it. (In summer the ham should be cooled in cold water, as the liquid then easily becomes sour.)
Remove the rind; press a towel against the lard to remove all dissolved fat.
Beat the egg white with a fork into a light foam, mix with mustard and sugar, and with this brush the ham's lard side.
Sprinkle the crushed rusks over, place the ham in a roasting pan and put in a warm oven to get a beautiful brown color, which takes about 1/2 hour.
Place on a large platter, garnish beautifully with greens and serve warm or cold with vegetables, prunes and filled apple halves. The ham bone is garnished with curled paper.

title: Kokt, kall lax (Cold Boiled Salmon, 18 servings)
description: Prepared with salmon, broth, and vinegar.

ingredients.name: For garnish: mayonnaise, capers or truffle, beets, tomatoes, lettuce, parsley, hard-boiled eggs
ingredients.sourceText: For garnish: mayonnaise, capers or truffle, beets, tomatoes, lettuce, parsley, hard-boiled eggs

steps: Cook the broth and prepare the salmon as in the previous recipe.
If the salmon is to be served on two platters, split it lengthwise into two halves and carefully remove the bone. Place the two halves with the bone in the cold broth and cook as in recipe 327.
Let the salmon cool in the broth.
From the broth prepare white and red aspic as in recipe 181.
Let a little of the white fish aspic set on the bottom of the platters where the salmon will be served. Place the salmon on top.
Remove the skin in 3 cm wide strips across the fish, leaving equal-width strips of skin in between.

Where the skin has been removed, spread mayonnaise mixed with a little white fish aspic and let it set. Garnish the mayonnaise with capers or truffle in attractive figures, such as fleurs-de-lis or royal crowns.
Garnish the remaining strips with white and red fish aspic piped through a fine decorating tube, and small slices of beets or tomatoes.
Garnish the platter with lettuce, parsley, hollowed-out tomatoes filled with vegetable salad, egg halves with decorated edges and aspic.
Serve with mayonnaise or remoulade sauce.

title: Kokt, salt kött (Boiled Salted Meat)
description: Prepared with beef and water.

ingredients.name: Outer or inner loin of beef, salted
ingredients.sourceText: Outer or inner loin of beef, salted

steps: If the meat has been salted for only 1½–2 weeks, it need not be soaked before cooking. Rinse the meat and place it in enough cold water to cover it well. Bring it rapidly to a boil, skim thoroughly, and let it boil for 15 minutes at 100°. Cool the broth to 82°–83° and keep the meat at this temperature for 3½ hours, or until tender. If serving cold, place the meat in a stone crock, pour the broth over it, and let it cool in the crock. The meat can be stored in the broth for several days. If the meat is heavily salted, soak it for 12–24 hours before cooking.

title: Kokt, salt oxtunga (Boiled Salted Ox Tongue)
description: Prepared with salt and water.
steps: The tongue, which should be lightly salted, is placed in chilled water for a couple of hours
Place in cold water, skim, and boil for 15 minutes at 100°
Cool the broth to 82°-83° and keep the tongue at this temperature for 3 1/2 hours, or until the skin can easily be removed
Place in a stone crock with flat bottom, pour the broth over, and let the tongue cool in it—it becomes juicier if cooled in the broth
If to be served warm, warm it in the broth after the skin is removed
If the tongue is very salty, it should soak in water for about 12 hours

title: Kokt, varm lax (Hot Boiled Salmon, 12 servings)
description: Prepared with salmon, broth, and vinegar.
steps: Pour the water and vinegar into a pot. Add the salt, scraped carrot cut into small pieces, peeled onion, bay leaf and parsley, and let the broth cook for 1 hour. Ten minutes before it is done, add the peppercorns.
Strain the broth through a fine sieve, taste and let cool.
Scale and clean the salmon without cutting too much, and wash well with a cloth dipped in cold water, then dry.
The salmon can be boiled whole, split lengthwise into two halves (the bone is removed but cooked with the fish) or cut into 3-4 cm thick slices.
Cook in the broth according to instructions in recipe 327.
Serve with hollandaise, mousseline, crayfish or shrimp sauce and small boiled potatoes.
Leftovers of boiled salmon can be used for mayonnaise (recipe 176), salad (recipe 177) or gratin (see sole gratin, recipe 377).

The soda is used during cooking for this same reason.
Kept in brine.
Served with beetroot.

description: Prepared with artichokes, salt, and water.
steps: Clean the artichokes by removing the stem and the lower hard leaves and cutting off the sharp prickles on the remaining leaves.
Rinse them well and tie them with string so they do not fall apart during cooking.
Place them in lightly salted boiling water, but only enough to cover them one-third of the way.
Boil them rapidly with a tight-fitting lid for approximately 15-20 minutes.
Place them on a warm sieve to drain and cut off the string.
Place the artichokes upside down on a warm platter with a folded napkin.
Serve with the same type of sauce as asparagus.

title: Kokta turska bönor (Boiled Turkish Beans)
description: Prepared with beans, water, and salt.
steps: The beans are cleaned and rinsed, allowed to drain on cloth, and cut into 4 mm. thick pieces, cut across (slightly on the diagonal).
They are placed in boiling, salted water and allowed to cook until tender. Excess liquid is then drained off and the beans are mixed with the parsley and cold butter.

Served with braised ham, boiled sausage and roasted meat.

title: Kokta Ägg (Boiled Eggs)
description: Prepared with eggs, salt, and water.
steps: Wash the eggs well before cooking; if the shells are spotted, rub them with salt or ash and rinse.
Place them in a steel basket or egg net and lower them into just enough boiling water to cover the eggs evenly. If too much water is used, the shells will crack easily.
Let the eggs boil slowly without a lid for approximately 3-3½ minutes; if soft-boiled eggs are desired with a hard white and runny yolk, boil for 5 minutes.
If the eggs are to be used for sauce or garnishing, boil them for 10 minutes.
Rinse the soft-boiled eggs quickly in cold water, dry them, and serve immediately. Leave the hard-boiled eggs in cold water for approximately 10 minutes so the shell will come off easily.

title: Kongresser (Almond-Filled Pastries)
description: A pastry dish made with sweet almonds, strawberry jam, and flour.
steps: Prepare the butter dough as in recipe no. 34, roll out thinly, cut with a round mold into cakes, and line small fluted pastry molds with it.
For the filling, dry the almonds in a cloth and grind them.
Whip the eggs and sugar for 20 minutes, then add the almonds.
Place a little jam in each mold, then fill the molds nearly to the rim with almond mixture.
Bake the pastries in a warm oven until the almond mixture feels dry when tested with a whisk.
Turn the pastries out, let cool, and serve with coffee or tea.

title: Korintkaka (Currant Cake)

ingredients.name: 2 msk. crushed rusks for the pan

Stir in the meat and mushrooms along with the beaten egg yolks and the rinsed gelatin dissolved in 1 msk. hot water.
Season the mixture with spices and treat as in recipe no. 49.
Serve the croquettes as a course with peas and poultry sauce.

title: Kroketter av tunga (Tongue Croquettes)
description: Prepared with tongue, celery, and leek.
steps: Let the tongue soak in cold water for a few hours, then scald in hot water and scrape well.
Place it in boiling salted water and skim the stock well when it comes to a boil, then add the prepared root vegetables and let the tongue cook slowly until tender, about 2 hours.
Remove the skin and let the tongue cool.
Cut the tongue into fine cubes.
Strain the stock, skim it, and mix 3 deciliters of it with the meat extract.
Fry the butter and flour for 2 minutes, add the stock and let the sauce cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tongue and finely chopped capers or olives together with the whipped egg yolks and the gelatin that has been rinsed and dissolved in 1 tablespoon hot water.
Season the mixture with spices and treat as in recipe no. 49.
Form the croquettes into oblong shapes.
Serve as a side course with peas or mixed vegetables.
